articles.title: De la euforia al vértigo: España se juega ante Japón su futuro en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Obligada a ganar para asegurar su pase (17.50 h TDP). Si vence y Alemania derrota a Mali, a cuartos • Si es segunda o tercera, a octavos • Y si es cuarta, a casa salvo triunfo africano
articles.summary: Obligada a ganar para asegurar su pase (17.50 h TDP). Si vence y Alemania derrota a Mali, a cuartos • Si es segunda o tercera, a octavos • Y si es cuarta, a casa salvo triunfo africano
articles.body: La inesperada, por sorprendente, derrota de España (7ª en el ranking FIBA) ante Mali (18ª), a la que siete días antes había aplastado por 39 puntos en un amistoso (97-58), la ha colocado de la noche a la mañana en el disparadero del Mundial. De confirmar su candidatura a las medallas tras arrollar en la primera jornada a la anfitriona Alemania (83-53), al batacazo ante el combinado africano (82-73) que la deja al borde del precipicio. Todo puede pasar a falta de la última jornada que se disputará este lunes en el Max-Schmeling-Halle (Berlín) con los dos partidos del grupo A a las 17.50 h: España-Japón y Mali-Alemania. Con los cuatro equipos igualados con una victoria y una derrota, todos pueden ocupar cualquier posición en función de los resultados que se den. Los tres primeros se clasificarán para los cruces: el líder, directamente a cuartos de final; el segundo y el tercero, a un cruce previo de octavos. Ese es el monumental lío en el que se ha metido España, un país de excesos en el que lo que un día es sublime al siguiente puede tornarse en catastrófico. Pero esta selección ni era el nuevo 'Dream Team' del baloncesto femenino tras la primera jornada ni es un desecho de tienta después de la segunda. Aunque algunos aventuraban, embriagados por la euforia de su estelar debut, que era la principal rival de Estados Unidos por el oro. Como si las potentísimas Francia y Australia no jugasen. Dentro de lo preocupante de esta situación tan incierta, lo más razonable es ver el vaso medio lleno, porque España depende de sí misma para clasificarse. Si gana a Japón se meterá en los cruces como primera o segunda, dependiendo del resultado del Alemania-Mali. Y si es como segunda, evitaría a Estados Unidos en una hipotética semifinal. E incluso en caso de derrota ante los nipones en el peor de los supuestos, podría acceder a octavos de final como tercera si las africanas derrotan a las anfitrionas. Lo más lógico, sin que eso signifique lanzar las campanas al vuelo, es que España se imponga a Japón, aunque el deporte es un territorio abonado para las sorpresas, como se vio ante Mali, donde lo previsible no siempre sucede y la coherencia puede mutar en incongruencia tras el salto inicial. Pero el sentido común, el juego colectivo, la experiencia, las estadísticas y los argumentos baloncestísticos de uno y otro dictan que España sobre el papel es mejor equipo que Japón. Y eso que la selección nipona, décima del ranking FIBA, no es ni mucho menos una perita en dulce. Quien así lo piense se equivoca y para darse cuenta de su error no tendría más que visionar -como ya hizo ayer la selección española- un resumen del partido que firmaron en su estreno mundialista para superar a Mali (102-97). Fue un partido en el que Japón batió el récord de triples en el campeonato con 20/35 (57,1%) y su jugadora Saki Hayashi el de triples en un partido del torneo con 9/15 (60%). España está avisada de dónde puede llegar el peligro de la selección asiática. Tomó buena nota de ello Alemania, que en la segunda jornada viendo el aluvión de triples nipón contra Mali, ató en corto a las tiradoras japonesas, de gatillo fácil, rebajando su porcentaje de triples a 3/27 (11%) anulando así su principal amenaza. Y fueron presa fácil para las germanas, que impusieron su mayor solidez y su físico (74-58). Alemania enseñó el camino del triunfo a España, que necesita recuperar su mejor versión tanto en lo colectivo como en lo individual para salir airosa de esta situación tan peliaguda en la que se ha metido. Urge que las de Miguel Méndez recuperen su confianza tras el palo ante Mali para volver a ser el equipo reconocible, competitivo, potente y fiable que es y no pareció ante las africanas. Si muestra su mejor cara, la que exhibió en su debut ante Alemania, España no tendrá problemas para tumbar a Japón. Pero si vuelve a sembrar las dudas, ya sea por cansancio, por falta de acierto exterior, o por dar medio metro de más a las peligrosísimas tiradoras niponas, podría pasar más apuros de los que desearía.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Unexpected Exchange With Italy Coach Goes Viral During Team USA Clash
articles.summary: The Caitlin Clark and Italy coach exchange had fans calling it ‘absolute comedy.’
articles.body:
Almost every WNBA fan waits for Caitlin Clark's sideline moments. Similarly, her recent exchange with Italy women's basketball head coach Andrea Capobianco caught the attention of eagle-eyed social media fans.

In their FIBA World Cup encounter on September 6, 2026, Team USA led Italy 13-8 with 2:03 remaining in the first quarter. But as two officials were debating a foul, the game came to a halt. When it came to speaking with a referee, Clark, who is often in the forefront of similar situations, got in on the action. Capobianco gave Clark one of his most animated reactions to date when he saw her. Now his reaction is making the rounds online.

The Mirror US reported that Capobianco said, "Non capisci, I seen you," fusing Italian and English when he addressed Clark , according to expert lip reader Nicola Hickling of LipReader Ltd. via Covers . According to Hickling, Clark's response was far more direct: "Stop complaining."

Either way, the online community had already started having a field day while watching the match live, as one X (formerly Twitter) user posted, "Caitlin rizzing the Italy coach 😭😭😭."

Another person joked, "He's confronting the wrong person 😂 Caitlin will argue with you."

Although Capobianco appeared to disagree with Clark on that particular point, the Italian head coach is wise enough not to ignore the brilliance of the Indiana Fever guard completely. This is because before Team USA's game against Italy, Capobianco had some kind words for Clark.

In a clip shared by Euro Women's Hoops on X, the Italian coach can be heard saying, "From a technical standpoint, I think Caitlin is incredible. From an image standpoint, she makes this sport even more enjoyable. Because, besides her ability to score, she makes everything she does look beautiful."

Nevertheless, fans were amused to see the whole Clark-Capobianco exchange, with some dubbing it "absolute comedy." Some even joked, saying that "caitlin gave bro his first smile of the night."

As Team USA fought to avoid its first loss at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in 20 years on Sunday, Clark had a rough night herself. She went scoreless from the field in her team's 55-52 win over Italy in Berlin. The Fever guard scored one point in the game and went 0-for-6 from the field. She also missed all three of her three-point attempts.

Clark played 19 minutes and recorded two turnovers, one steal, one assist, and four rebounds. Interestingly, the 24-year-old Team USA guard had never before gone an entire game without making a field goal at the WNBA or collegiate level. Her previous career low was three points on 1-of-10 shooting for Indiana against the New York Liberty in June 2024.

Together, Clark, Kahleah Cooper, and Breanna Stewart shot 1-for-19 from the field during the Sunday game. Overall, Stewart and Clark shot 1-for-15 from the field.

On Sunday, Team USA's remarkable winning streak was nearly over. With just 55 points against Italy, Team USA had its lowest scoring total since 1971.

Team USA hit 1-of-12 from three-point range and 29 percent from the field. Many believe Kara Lawson's team's 32-game winning streak could have ended if they hadn't had a significant lead in the charity stripe.

Per ESPN , speaking after the narrow win over Italy, Team USA head coach Lawson said, "We've seen that through the tournament that every game feels like a dogfight. It's really hard. On any given night, if you're not prepared to play, you'll lose."

The tight victory, in spite of the scare, guaranteed Team USA's place in the knockout round and increased the unprecedented World Cup winning streak to 32 games.

Clark shot 0-of-6 from the floor, finishing with one point, four rebounds, one assist and one steal. That followed a record-setting performance in Team USA's opener.

As the final score would indicate, Clark was far from the only U.S. player who struggled against the Italians. The United States' overall output was its lowest at the World Cup since 1971, and it shot 28.6 percent overall while having more turnovers (14) than assists (11).

For as much talent as Team USA has from top to bottom, A'ja Wilson's absence looms large. The score might've looked much different if the four-time WNBA MVP had been stationed in the paint.

The United States closes out the group phase Monday against Czechia, and it could be a great opportunity for Clark and others who lack a lot of international experience.

The Americans have already qualified for the quarterfinals by virtue of winning Group D. With little at stake, coach Kara Lawson may choose to rest her usual starters ahead of the knockout stage. In that case, Clark would be getting plenty of playing time.

articles.title: Japón - España en directo | Última hora de Mundial Femenino en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Ahora España tendrá dos días de descanso hasta el partido de cuartos de final. El rival saldrá del Australia contra el tercero del grupo D, a decidir
articles.body:
Última hora del Japón - España en directo:

¡¡¡Muuuuy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la última jornada de la fase de grupos del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto 2026 de Alemania !!! Último día de infarto para las cuatro selecciones que conforman este grupo A y que llegan empatadas (1-1) tras el batacazo de España ante Mali (82-73) el pasado sábado.

Las de Miguel Méndez afrontan esta primera final ante Japón con la obligación de ganar si no quiere sustos, aunque existe un escenario en el que una derrota también la clasificaría para octavos de final. España juega ante una selección nipona que sucumbió en la última jornada ante Alemania (74-58) , pero que venció a Mali (102-97) en una exhibición de triples . Un nuevo récord de 20 lanzamientos de tres de 35 intentos , con un tremendo 9/15 para Saki Hayashi .

España , a la que ya se le escapó el encuentro ante Mali por esa vía, deberá tener cuidado con uno de los puntos fuertes de las japonesas . Además, también deberá mejorar sus porcentajes en este aspecto. Pasó de un 14/28 (50%) en triples ante Alemania al 4/22 (18%) contra las africanas . El tiro libre también está siendo una piedra en la rueda de la Selección ; un 41% el primer día y un 53% el segundo.

Pese al lío formado entre los cuatro combinados, las cuentas son claras , donde las de Méndez tienen posibilidad de ocupar todas las posiciones. Si España gana hoy, será primera de grupo si Alemania hace lo propio con Mali ; en cambio, será segunda si las africanas también dan la sorpresa ante las anfitrionas . Los otros dos escenarios llegarían con la derrota de España ; si Mali gana a Alemania se salvaría y entraría como tercera , pero si las europeas vencieran a la verduga de la Selección serían cuartas y quedarían eliminadas.

Es decir, España tendrá que tener un ojo puesto en el otro partido que se juega de manera simultánea, ya que el resultado del Alemania-Mali influye directamente en la posición que ocupará. Si las de Méndez acaban primeras , jugarán directamente los cuartos el jueves 10 de septiembre . Pero si quedan segundas o terceras , tendrán menos descanso ya que jugarían una ronda más y disputarían los octavos de final en el día de mañana.

En definitiva, partido vital el que tiene la Selección esta tarde en Berlín . El Max Schmeling volverá a ser testigo de un nuevo encuentro de España , y nosotros, volveremos a contártelo con todo tipo de detalle. Esta tarde, desde las 17.50 horas , la Selección española se enfrenta a Japón para seguir con vida en este Mundial en el que hay tanta ilusión puesta, y lo viviremos como siempre, aquí, en MARCA .

articles.title: Thomas Walkup remata el colosal proyecto del Dubái Basketball
articles.standfirst: El equipo de los emiratos saca al base del Olympiacos, campeón de la Euroliga, con un contrato por tres temporadas y 9,6 millones de dólares
articles.summary: El equipo de los emiratos saca al base del Olympiacos, campeón de la Euroliga, con un contrato por tres temporadas y 9,6 millones de dólares
articles.body: El Dubái Basketball ha rematado su ambicioso segundo proyecto en la Euroliga con la incorporación de Thomas Walkup, base de 1,95 metros y 33 años que procede del Oympiacos, con el que se proclamó campeón de Europa la temporada pasada con promedios de 5,3 puntos, 2,6 rebotes, 5,7 asistencias y 0,9 robos. "Thomas es un fichaje muy importante para Dubai Basketball y otro paso adelante en la dirección que queremos tomar como club. Su conocimiento del juego, su competitividad y su capacidad para hacer mejores a los jugadores que le rodean serán extremadamente valiosos para nuestro equipo", valora Dejan Kamenjasevic, presidente de un Dubái Basketball que va con todo en busca de la Final Four. El equipo de los emiratos, que tendrá a Xavi Pascual en su banquillo, perseguía el fichaje del base desde hace tiempo y finalmente lo ha conseguido a golpe de talonario. Ha conseguido sacar al base de El Pireo pagando 2,6 millones de dólares y le ha puesto un contrato de 9,6 millones por tres campañas. Se hace así con uno de los bases más sólidos de la Euroliga en los últimos años y un defensor contrastado. La incorporación de Walkup se suma a las del exazulgrana Toko Shengelia, el exbaskonista Mamadi Diakite, Davion Mintz, Elie Okobo y Jaron Blossomgame. También estuvo cerca de contratar a Alpha Diallo, el mejor defensor de la Euroliga, aunque finalmente se marchó a los Nuggets. Todas esos fichajes se suman a las estrellas con las que ya contaba el conjunto emiratí: Dzanan Musa, McKinley Wright, Dwayne Bacon, Justin Anderson, Davis Bertans, Mfiondu Kabengele, Filip Petrusev... Hasta 18 jugadores tendrá Pascual a su disposición. Además, pensando en el futuro, el equipo de Dubái ha atado este verano a Kevin Kokila, que jugará en la Virtus Bolonia; a Yannick Kraag, que seguirá en el Asisa Joventut; Simonas Lukosius, que se irá al Unicaja; e incluso a Soumaila Keita, pívot maliense de 15 años y 2,12 metros que militaba en el Casademont Zaragoza.

articles.title: El camino de España en el Mundial: posibles cuartos ante Australia... y Estados Unidos en semifinales
articles.standfirst: La selección consigue el liderato del grupo, pero irá por el mismo lado del cuadro que las estadounidenses, favoritas al oro
articles.summary: La selección consigue el liderato del grupo, pero irá por el mismo lado del cuadro que las estadounidenses, favoritas al oro
articles.body: Después de las complicaciones que creó la sorprendente derrota ante Mali, la selección femenina consiguió el primer objetivo en el Mundial: el liderato del grupo. La victoria ante Japón (59-79) sumada al triunfo de Alemania (83-58) le dio la primera plaza. Eso le permite acceder directamente a cuartos de final sin necesidad de disputar un peligroso play-in de octavos. España no jugará ya hasta este jueves, cuando afronte esos cuartos de final. El rival saldrá del duelo entre Australia (C2) y el perdedor del Italia-China (D3) que cerrará la fase de grupos. Ese play-in se jugará este miércoles, con lo que el rival de la selección no tendrá descanso antes del cruce. Si el combinado de Miguel Méndez supera esos cuartos de final, se mediría en semifinales a Estados Unidos, que tiene garantizado el liderato de su grupo a falta del último partido. Pese al sufrido triunfo ante Italia, las estadounidenses siguen siendo las grandes favoritas al oro.

articles.title: España sufre, acaba líder y se mete en cuartos de forma directa
articles.standfirst: Gana a Japón en un partido con mucha tensión por lo que había en juego y en el que brilla Iyana Martín
articles.summary: Gana a Japón en un partido con mucha tensión por lo que había en juego y en el que brilla Iyana Martín
articles.body: España sacó adelante un complicadísimo partido ante Japón, 59-79, y con ello no solo se metió en la segunda fase, sino que lo hizo como líder de grupo y, por lo tanto, de forma directa para los cuartos de final del jueves, evitando el play-in de octavos. Pero tuvo que sufrir, y mucho. Es posible que Estados Unidos tenga a Caitlin Clark, pero España tiene una jugadora que va para superestrella y no tiene tanto que envidiarla. Iyana Martín iluminó el camino de la selección ante Japón, sobre todo en una primera parte a la que le sobraron los últimos dos minutos. Como ante Mali. Como se esperaba, Japón lo iba a fiar todo a su triple y a cortar el ritmo de España. En lo primero no estuvieron bien, 4/13 al descanso, 7/30 total. España incluso mejoraba eso, 4/11 y 8/25. Lo segundo se vio cuando en el primer cuarto ya sumaban 10 faltas y, a dos minutos para el final, las 12 jugadoras ya llevaban al menos una falta, eso sí, muy repartida. España, más entonada que ante Mali, llegó al final del primer cuarto con ventaja, 15-23, que quedó reducida por el 7-1 de Japón a la salida del segundo acto. Pero a 3:11 para el final, las de Méndez rompían el partido, 24-34, gracias a una canasta de mucho talento de Iyana. Y de nuevo la pájara de España. En apenas dos minutos la selección perdió su ventaja, 36-39 al descanso, con un parcial nipón de 12-5. Con las jugadoras en el vestuario, España sabía que solo le valía ganar el partido porque en el Uber Arena Alemania ganaba 49-32 a Mali. España salió más sólida en la reanudación y volvió a rondar los 10 de ventaja, 36-46 a 7:38 tras una canasta de Fam. Eran momentos en los que la selección era superior en el juego interior y, sobre todo, en la defensa, tratando de evitar los tiros cómodos de las japonesas. Las niponas, lejos de rendirse, intentaron volver al partido y lo hicieron con un par de triples para acercarse, 47-53 a 1:50, cuando Alemania ya ganaba por 22 a Mali. Una canasta de Carrera devolvió cierta tranquilidad a España, 48-57, cuando acababa el tercer episodio del partido. Japón jugaba sin la presión de la eliminación, porque la victoria alemana las clasificaba, como poco, en tercera posición. España, sin embargo, mostraba más tensión en sus gestos y en su juego. Pero las veteranas están para añadir tranquilidad y, tras dos fallos en el tiro libre, María Conde clavó un triple que devolvió los 10, 50-60, y a partir de ahí España ya controlaba el choque con la maravillosa Iyana a los mandos. Con Japón a la desesperada, España golpeó hasta una máxima de 15, 57-72, a dos minutos. Con el partido ganado, la selección aumentó esa máxima para un marcador que no resumió el enorme sufrimiento que pasó España para ganar y meterse directamente para los cuartos de final. Iyana no sólo guió con su juego a España hasta los cuartos, sino que fue la mejor anotadora, 20 puntos. Awa Fam hizo un doble-doble, 16+10 y Conde acabó con 9 puntos.

articles.title: Tigers' Jack Flaherty 'feeling good' after rehab appearance
articles.summary: The Tigers' Jack Flaherty threw 1⅓ scoreless innings for Triple-A Toledo, giving up a hit with a walk and two strikeouts at Fifth Third Field.
articles.body:
DETROIT — After throwing a bullpen session late last week, the logical next step for Tigers right-hander Jack Flaherty was to start his rehab assignment, getting him one step closer to returning the Tigers' rotation.

That next step took place Sunday evening, as Flaherty threw 1⅓ scoreless innings for Triple-A Toledo, giving up a hit with a walk and two strikeouts at Fifth Third Field.

"I think he came out feeling good and also a little critical of how his mechanics were and how he executed," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said Monday, Sept. 7, shortly before the Tigers hosted Minnesota in the first of three games at Comerica Park. "He had a walk in there and he ended up getting second (inning), which his nice.

"But I think the encouraging part is the recovery was good."

Flaherty has been out since July 21 with a flexor tendon strain and his been steadily working his way back.

On Sunday, he threw 19 pitches, allowing a one-out double in the first inning before issuing a two-out walk. He worked his way out of trouble with a strikeout to end the inning then returned for the top of the second, getting a groundout on the first pitch.

That was it, as Flaherty was pulled and now the Tigers plan the next step.

"He will do something in the next five days, or after five days," Hinch said, "kind of on the same cadence where he will throw a (bullpen session) and then we'll decide kind of what's next for him. (It could be) another outing or we can build some volume in a (simulated) game. We have a couple options, but we haven't finalized what the plan is.

"The first step was here today he felt great, and that's good."

Flaherty, who will be a free agent after the season, last pitched on July 20 against the Chicago Cubs. He is 3-8 this season with a 4.59 ERA in 19 starts over 86⅓ innings.

While the focus has shifted away from a realistic push for the playoffs over the final few weeks of the season, the Tigers are taking advantage of the opportunities offered some of their young, promising talent.

In Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Guardians , six rookies were in the starting lineup, and that's not necessarily a bad thing.

"That's a good step for those guys to get that type of experience and that type of challenge," Hinch said of facing Guardians starter Gavin Williams . "We've asked a lot of these guys to make pretty sizeable jumps when you look at young guys like ( John ) Peck , like ( Brett ) Callahan that are coming up pretty quickly.

"I'm encouraged by the fact guys are holding they're own. They're also seeing the challenge of the every day here. There are no easy days in the big leagues."

▶ First pitch: 6:40 p.m. Tuesday, Comerica Park, Detroit

▶ RHP Drew Anderson (4-5, 3.73), Tigers: This will be the second straight start Anderson makes against the Twins and right-hander Dean Kremer . In that start, Anderson left with the lead after going 5⅔ innings, giving up three hits and two runs (one earned) while striking out five.

▶ RHP Dean Kremer (2-5, 5.81), Twins: Kremer lasted only four innings in last week's start against the Tigers, allowing four runs and six hits as the Tigers went on to win, 11-6 in 12 innings. It was the second straight rough outing for Kremer, who gave up six runs in a loss to the White Sox on Aug. 28. This will be his fifth career start against Detroit and his third this season, the first coming while with the Baltimore Orioles.

articles.title: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter turns $427 NCAA suspension into powerful cancer research fundraiser
articles.summary: Arion Carter is donating $427 per tackle to Nashville cancer charities after his girlfriend Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer.
articles.body: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter walked out of the tunnel as the Vols’ sole captain during their home opener this past weekend, even though he was not suited up for the game. Amid the controversial decisions surrounding former professional athletes returning to college athletics, Carter accepted his punishment when he could have easily sought help from a local judge to create a path back onto the field. Following the 2025 season, the Vols linebacker decided to declare for the 2026 NFL Draft and leave Tennessee to pursue his professional dreams. TENNESSEE COACH UNLOADS ON NCAA'S 'BULLS–T', AFTER STAR LINEBACKER SUSPENDED FOR OUTDATED RULE Unfortunately, Carter found out he was dealing with a foot injury that would require him to have surgery and miss out on preparations for the upcoming draft. So, he made the decision to return to college. There were a few complications. Carter accepted $427 from an agent to cover a flight to a workout, and he knew his return to Tennessee could lead to an NCAA suspension. The NCAA's punishment came in the form of a one-game suspension that was initially set to keep the star linebacker out for the opening three games of the season. With all of the chaos surrounding college athletics — from state courtrooms to federal court — Carter handled the situation with the utmost respect. Carter is turning NCAA suspension into a fundraiser for cancer research Arion's girlfriend is currently in the middle of her own battle with cancer. To show his support, Carter recently shaved his head for the woman he loves. Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer earlier this year. She lives in the Nashville area, where she works as an ICU nurse at a local hospital. But now, he's also raising money for cancer research with his play on the field. First reported by Austin Price of VolQuest, Arion Carter will donate $427 for each tackle that he makes this season to Nashville area charities that support women struggling to pay bills during their battles with cancer. He is turning the $427 plane ticket reimbursement into something positive for the community, further demonstrating the character of a young man who has handled this entire ordeal with tremendous class. Wearing a "Team Jesus" shirt on Monday, Carter explained how he is turning a negative situation into a positive one. "It also goes back to my mom. articles.body:
Team USA found its scoring touch for a 105-64 win over Czechia in its group play matchup at the FIBA Women's World Cup in Berlin on Monday.

The U.S. had already qualified for the quarterfinals of the tournament after winning its first two games in Group D competition. Meanwhile, Czechia was eliminated in the group stage after losing its first two games.

Breanna Stewart was hot from the start, notching 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting in the first quarter. She finished with 19 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists. Napheesa Collier, Jackie Young and Angel Reese each added 12 points. Collier also grabbed seven boards while Reese registered six in the win.

Every USA player scored at least one basket after Sonia Citron hit a baseline jumper at the end of the third. Citron finished with 10 points, as did Paige Bueckers. Caitlin Clark added 9 points and 7 assists, shooting 1-for-6 on 3-pointers.

The Americans only had one player score in double figures in Sunday's 55-52 win over Italy with Jackie Young tallying 10 points.

Team USA ended the first quarter with a 29-15 lead, shooting 52% from the floor. That was significantly encouraging after a 29% team shooting performance versus Italy.

The U.S. went ahead by 21 points with a 17-9 run through the first seven minutes of the second quarter and eventually took a 57-33 lead into halftime. That was more points than USA scored in Sunday's entire game.

The onslaught continued in the third quarter with Team USA opening up a 32-point margin after a 14-3 run.

Long-range shooting is still an issue for the Americans, who shot 28% (7 for 25) on 3-pointers. That was an improvement over the 1-for-12 (8%) effort versus Italy , but no USA player hit more than one shot from behind the arc against Czechia.

Eliska Joklova led Czechia with 19 points, hitting 11-of-14 free throws. She was the only Czechian player to reach double figures, though Julie Pospisilova scored nine while Natalie Stoupalova and Veronika Vorackova each got eight points.

Team USA has already qualified for the quarterfinals with three wins in Group D play. Those include a 94-61 win over China to open the tournament, along with the victory versus Italy. The Americans will face the winner of Tuesday's Hungary-Japan matchup on Thursday.

articles.title: Francia es el coco
articles.standfirst: La selección gala ha arrollado en la primera fase, lidera las principales estadísticas y es la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: La selección gala ha arrollado en la primera fase, lidera las principales estadísticas y es la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos
articles.body: Finalizada la primera fase, puede decirse que Francia es el coco del Mundial. Después de los tres primeros encuentros, la selección gala ha demostrado ser lo que se esperaba de ella antes del campeonato. Es un equipo mayúsculo. Tiene físico, calidad, amplitud, está trabajado, tiene estrellas... Y hambre. Antes de los cruces, cerró su grupo aplastando a Nigeria por 56-111 con récord de triples en un Mundial Femenino: 22/40. Si ya se consideraba a Francia como la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos (72-0 marcha desde 2006 en torneos a nivel planetario), el potencial que ha exhibido y las debilidades que han mostrado las norteamericanas reafirman esa sensación. Quizás puedan completar en Berlín la revolución que se quedaron a un paso de consumar en los Juegos de París, cuando perdieron la final por 67-66. Francia ha terminado como el mejor equipo de la fase de grupos dominando casi todas las estadísticas importantes. Ha sido líder en puntos (101,7), tiros de dos (66,7%), triples (48,5%), asistencias (26,7), recuperaciones (13,7) y valoración (132,7) y segunda en tiros libres (79,2%). Cifras aplastantes. "Este grupo, este equipo, está en otro nivel", asegura Gabby Williams, uno de los referentes ofensivos de la selección gala. La alero de 1,80 metros de las Golden State Valkyries es la máxima anotadora de lo que va de Mundial con 18,7 puntos de media y un sensacional 55% desde el triple. En valoración, está igualada con Emma Meesseman en lo alto de la estadística con 23,3 créditos, aunque ella juega 22,5 minutos por partido y la belga 31,2. Williams considera que "las francesas siempre han tenido mucho talento, pero la cultura ha cambiado. Ahora jugamos con intensidad. No importa lo talentosos que seamos. Si no lo das todo en la cancha, te van a sacar. No nos importa el marcador. No nos importa contra quién juguemos. Siempre tenemos que aportar la misma energía". Además, cree que "hay mucho talento en el banquillo". Tanto que nadie en la selección juega más de 24 minutos de media. También es un referente Marine Johannes, escolta de 1,78 que milita en las New York Liberty junto a Raquel Carrera. Es una fábrica andante de highlights. Las canastas imposibles son cosa suya. Hasta LeBron James alucinó con una serie de triples desequilibrados, en carrera o a una pierna que hizo hace tres años en un partido de WNBA. Es letal desde el arco: 52,0%. Y hasta ahora se está comportando con una regularidad propia de un reloj suizo: 17 puntos en cada uno de los tres encuentros que ha disputado. "Estamos contentas con cómo estamos jugando ahora mismo. Estamos compartiendo el balón, jugando una buena defensa para poder correr la cancha. Somos bastante buenas cuando movemos el balón rápidamente", dice Johannes. Las 26,7 asistencias que su equipo da por encuentro es una cifra escandalosa que muestra generosidad y capacidad para circular la pelota a tanta velocidad que los rivales se encuentran persiguiendo sombras. La tercera pata del sólido banco francés es Dominique Malonga, pívot de 1,97 que es compañera de Awa Fam en Seattle. Capaz de hacer mates, la jugadora nacida en senegal, es una fuerza de la naturaleza que se impone en la pintura. Nadie tiene mejor porcentaje que ella en tiros de dos puntos en este Mundial (73,7%). Hacerle llegar el balón bajo el aro es casi asegurar la canasta. Francia, como líder de su grupo, está ya en cuartos de final. Allí se medirá al ganador del duelo entre Puerto Rico y China. Favoritísima sea cual sea su rival. En semifinales, probablemente, se mediría a Bélgica. Es el camino hacia las medallas. La selección gala no consigue subir a un podio en un Mundial Femenino desde la primera edición, allá por 1953, cuando se colgó el bronce. Viendo su rendimiento, aspira a todo. Sí, incluso a acabar el trabajo que dejó a medias en París 2024.

articles.title: FSU-SMU game turns into old-school football after stadium power outage wipes out in-game communication
articles.summary: A power outage plunged Doak Campbell Stadium into darkness minutes before kickoff, forcing SMU and Florida State to play without communications.
articles.body: Just when we thought the college football weekend couldn’t get any crazier, a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium on the campus of Florida State sent school officials into a frenzy on Monday night in Tallahassee. Minutes before SMU and FSU were set to close out Labor Day weekend with there ACC game to finish week one, the lights went out inside the stadium that forced both teams back into the locker room. The game was scheduled to kickoff at 7:39 p.m. ET, but a power surge sent the stadium into darkness just as both teams had taking the field. Trust me, the jokes could write themselves for Florida State, but this unfortunate set of circumstances for everyone involved turned into a chaotic night. A very critical decision awaited, knowing there would also be no official replay during the game if both schools decided to play Both SMU and FSU decided to play the game without half the stadium having power . Every twenty minutes, officials from both schools and ACC commissioner Jim Phillips were meeting to discuss possible outcomes if they weren’t able to play the game on Monday night. For the fans, credit to them for sticking around through the madness, with games being played in the stands and the Florida State marching band trying their best to keep them all engaged. But, this was a mess. At 8:45 ET, following a third meeting between officials, the decision was made to play the game on Monday night without any type of communications. This included helmet-to-helmet comms, communication between coordinators or iPad usage along the sideline. Simply put, both teams decided to go full old-school tonight in Tallahassee. MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED The officials were having to practice hand signals with the coaches from both teams at 9:06 p.m. ET, while stadium officials were praying that the power would be fully-restored by the second half at the very least. No sideline communication for either team during the game I've seen some things covering this sport, but tonight is up their on the list on wildest events that have taken place in the past twenty years on the field. Both teams decided it would be a wise move to play without communications that are key for everyone involved in a college football game. And, sources told OutKick that there would have been an ample amount of problems for SMU to play this game on Tuesday. The Mustangs host UC Davis on Saturday, while the Seminoles have the weekend off. So, pushing this game back a day might have been the smart move, but would have been challenging for Rhett Lashlee and his football program. Also, you cannot just reschedule the game for later in the season for obvious reasons. The outcome was crucial for Florida State head coach Mike Norvell, who was already feeling the heat coming into the season. SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee noted that his team had not practiced without coach-to-player communication in over two years, so tonight was the first time since 2024 that he had not been in communication with his quarterback during a game. articles.body: Luka Doncic spent part of his offseason showing his new Los Angeles Lakers teammates where he grew up, hosting a minicamp in Slovenia after a roster shakeup that saw LeBron James depart. The trip mixed basketball, golf and downtime, all aimed at building chemistry before the 2026-27 season tips off.Fellow Slovenian Sasha Vujacic watched it thoroughly and came away impressed, while Lakers legend Robert Horry is not ready to hand out grades just yet. Their reactions frame a Lakers team still searching for its identity.Sasha Vujacic gives honest verdict on Luka DoncicLuka Doncic flew his new teammates out to Slovenia this summer, giving them a firsthand look at his home country before the grind of an NBA season sets in. Vujacic, who won two titles with the Lakers, sat down with ESPN Los Angeles and broke down what stood out most from the trip.Vujacic said the leadership has been obvious. He pointed to how Doncic opened up his home country to guys he had just started playing with, calling it a sign that his new teammate finally feels like a true Laker. "That's always great to see," Vujacic said.“It’s been there and what Luka has been doing, he’s showing the leadership. I’m very excited about this year. I think he’s finally a Laker, Laker. And him and AR and the team that we have, I can’t wait to watch it and for him to bring the team to Slovenia to show them where he comes from, to show everybody what Slovenia is all about,” Vujacic shared.“I think they have a better understanding of what it means for him to be in L.A. and through his journey how important it is to win.”Collin Sexton and Kevon Looney also came back from Slovenia with good things to say about their new teammate. Both players praised how welcoming Doncic had been, a detail that matters for a roster trying to gel fast after losing LeBron James.Former Lakers star Robert Horry has a different opinion on Luka DoncicThe Lakers enter the season with a roster that looks almost nothing like last year's group. Kessler, at 7-foot-2, is expected to anchor the frontcourt and protect the rim, while Grimes and Sexton add scoring depth off the bench.Doncic and Austin Reaves anchored the offense a season ago, with Doncic putting up a league-high 33.5 points a game. articles.title: Aari McDonald signs with Minnesota Lynx
articles.summary: It’s been a long time since former Arizona star Aari McDonald played in a WNBA game. That has come to an end with the first-place Minnesota Lynx announcing h...
articles.body:
It's been a long time since former Arizona star Aari McDonald played in a WNBA game. That has come to an end with the first-place Minnesota Lynx announcing her signing on Monday afternoon.

McDonald was injured last August while playing for the Indiana Fever. She tried to come back by playing in the Unrivaled 3×3 league during the WNBA offseason, but she was again sidelined by injury. As WNBA training camp approached this year, she said she would not be in camp but she would return this season. It took a while, but now she's not only returning, but she's doing it with the best team in the league.

The Lynx lead the WNBA standings with a 31-9 record and four games left in the regular season. The league returns to play on Sept. 18 after a break for the FIBA Women's World Cup where many top players are representing their countries. That event runs from Sept. 4-13, but the league shut down on Aug. 31.

McDonald sat out a large chunk of last season after being waived by the LA Sparks in training camp. She eventually landed with the Indiana Fever, where she quickly became a fan favorite of the passionate fan base and a fixture in the local community.

She averaged 9.8 points on 42.9 percent shooting, 4.7 assists, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.3 steals in 26.3 minutes per game for Indiana last season. She appeared in 20 games with 13 starts. It was a career high in games started, minutes per game, field goal percentage, assists per game, and rebounds per game.

Over the course of her career, she has averaged 8.8 points on 39.5 percent shooting, 3.1 assists, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals in 22.3 minutes per game. She has made 136 appearances and 42 starts for three different teams.

McDonald was drafted third in the 2021 draft by the Atlanta Dream just weeks after leading Arizona to its first and only national championship appearance. The Wildcats fell to Stanford by one point after dismissing UConn in the national semifinal.

During her time with Arizona, she won the 2020 Ann Meyers Drysdale award, the 2020 and 2021 Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year award, and the 2021 Pac-12 Player of the Year award. She joined Arizona's Ring of Honor the year after she turned pro.

Her time with the Minnesota will be her third time being on a playoff team, although she was injured when Indiana made last year's playoffs. She made two playoff appearances with the Atlanta Dream in 2023.

McDonald was also recently announced as an addition to Melikgazi Kayseri Basketbol in the Turkish KBSL for the 2026-27 season. The team will be looking to make a turnaround this year after finishing 6-14 in the KBSL last year. They fell to Fenerbahçe in the quarterfinals of the league playoffs. The organization had its best run during the early-to-mid 2010s when it was a quarterfinalist in EuroLeague (2013-14), the EuroCup runners-up three times, and the runner-up in the KBSL (2014-15).

McDonald's last season overseas was spent in China during the 2024-25 season. She spent the season before that in Australia where she was the league scoring champion with 19.8 ppg and helped her team reach the WNBL Grand Final. Her team, the Perth Lynx, finished as the WNBL runner-up.

articles.title: "Nuestros aficionados nos insultaban y nos escupían y en el vestuario todos se peleaban"
articles.standfirst: Marius Grigonis, ex del Panathinaikos, relata el caótico ambiente que reina en el equipo ateniense y el fanatismo extremo de sus aficionados
articles.summary: Marius Grigonis, ex del Panathinaikos, relata el caótico ambiente que reina en el equipo ateniense y el fanatismo extremo de sus aficionados
articles.body: Marius Grigonis ha regresado al Zalgiris Kaunas después de cuatro temporadas (2022-26) en el Panathinaikos y lo hace dejando tras de sí un testimonio que retrata con crudeza la particular realidad del gigante ateniense. En una entrevista concedida a la página web oficial del Zalgiris, el internacional lituano define su experiencia en Grecia como un "caos organizado", una montaña rusa capaz de llevarle del infierno al cielo en apenas unos meses. De los insultos y los escupitajos de los aficionados a ser llevado a hombros tras conquistar la Euroliga. "Un año te insultaban y al siguiente te llevaban a hombros porque habíamos ganado la Euroliga", resume Grigonis para explicar la dimensión de los extremos que vivió en Atenas. Y si hay un elemento que le dejó especialmente marcado fue el fanatismo de una afición que, según relata, supera incluso los límites que se atribuyen tradicionalmente a la hinchada del Zalgiris. "Hablamos de fanatismo en Kaunas y Zalgiris, pero allí todo es otro nivel", asegura. "Están realmente locos. Ni siquiera necesitan beber cerveza para ser así. Simplemente son así", relata el escolta. Grigonis recuerda sus primeros meses en un Panathinaikos todavía muy alejado del campeón de Europa en el que acabaría convirtiéndose: "Nuestros propios aficionados nos insultaban. Nos escupían. Caminabas por la calle y la gente te decía cosas". Un ambiente asfixiante que reflejaba también lo que sucedía dentro del vestuario: "Todos se peleaban y se insultaban", rememora. En ese escenario aparece la figura del entrenador Ergin Ataman, con quien Grigonis dibuja una relación inexistente. "Me gustaría que encontraran al menos un jugador que tenga una buena relación con él. Se distancia completamente de los jugadores. Él elige esa postura. No hay ninguna comunicación". Una declaración demoledora que apunta directamente al peculiar método de gestión de Ataman y que según Grigonis hacía imposible mantener una conversación normal con él: "Con Ataman, no funciona así". La última temporada fue, además, el mejor ejemplo de esa desconexión. Después de una larga ausencia por sus problemas de espalda, Grigonis regresó a la dinámica del equipo, pero su protagonismo en la Euroliga quedó reducido a apenas cinco minutos por partido: "Salía del entrenamiento, me iba a casa y luego recibía una llamada: “Ven al aeropuerto. Tienes que viajar para el partido". Y no era una excepción. "O llegaba al vestuario y, 25 minutos antes del partido, me traían el uniforme y me decían que me necesitaban". La improvisación y el caos reinaban en el equipo. Grigonis admite que la situación le llevó a quejarse y expresar su malestar, pero sin dejar de comportarse con profesionalidad. "Lo veía así: estoy aquí y voy a intentar hacer mi trabajo. Mi contrato es para ayudar al equipo. Claro que me quejé mucho y di mi opinión, pero cuando me necesitaron, estuve listo". La paradoja es que todo aquel caos terminó desembocando en el mayor éxito posible. El Panathinaikos pasó de aquel vestuario fracturado, de los insultos y de la hostilidad de sus propios aficionados a construir una plantilla repleta de estrellas y conquistar la Euroliga apenas un año después. Grigonis vivió las dos caras de una misma pasión: la que puede convertir al jugador en el enemigo público número uno y, poco después, elevarlo a los altares. Así es el Panathinaikos, el club en el que la línea que separa el éxtasis del cataclismo es muy delgada.

articles.title: El Barça pierde más de 17 millones en 2025-2026 y factura un 12% menos
articles.standfirst: La sección azulgrana ingresó un 7,1% menos, y un total de 19,5 millones, mientras los gastos de personal alcanzaron 28,9 millones
articles.summary: La sección azulgrana ingresó un 7,1% menos, y un total de 19,5 millones, mientras los gastos de personal alcanzaron 28,9 millones
articles.body: El Barça de baloncesto recorta sus pérdidas pese a reducir su negocio en una temporada aciaga en lo deportivo. La sección azulgrana redujo un 7,1% su cifra de negocio, hasta 19,5 millones de euros. Pese a ello, redujo sus pérdidas un 13,9%, hasta 17,7 millones de euros, gracias a que redujo su masa salarial, que es donde se encuentra el principal factor de presión en sus cuentas. El club blaugrana destinó 28,9 millones de euros a salarios, casi 3 millones menos que en la temporada 2024-2025. Fue en la facturación por competiciones donde más redujo su negocio. En un año en que no logró el pase a la Final Four de la Euroliga y en el cayó en semifinales de la Copa y en la final de la ACB, la sección de la canasta facturó 5,5 millones por méritos deportivos, un 12,4% menos interanual. La televisión, por su parte, aportó 4,5 millones, un 6% menos. El audiovisual se mantuvo como la tercera fuente de ingresos de la sección, con cerca de una cuarta parte de la facturación ordinaria. El patrocinio continuó siendo la principal fuente de ingresos del Barça de baloncesto, aunque también retrocedieron durante el ejercicio. Esta partida aportó 8,6 millones de euros, un 5,3% menos que el año anterior. La actividad comercial representa alrededor del 44% de la cifra de negocio de la sección. El descenso de esta vía de ingresos contribuyó a que la facturación ordinaria del equipo se situara por debajo de los 20 millones de euros. La única partida recurrente que creció fue la de abonados y socios, que pasó de 0,85 millones a 0,91 millones, un 6,2% más. Se espera que esta línea de negocio dé un salto en cuanto el Nou Palau Blaugrana esté listo, presumiblemente, de cara a 2029. Contará con 15.000 espectadores para partidos de baloncesto y un aforo de hasta 20.000 personas para conciertos. El principal desequilibrio de la cuenta de resultados está en los gastos de personal. La sección destinó 28,9 millones de euros a esta partida, un 8,7% menos interanual, pero todavía muy por encima de los ingresos generados por el equipo. La mayor parte corresponde al personal deportivo, con 28 millones de euros. A la plantilla de oficinas destinó menos de un millón de euros. Es decir, por cada euro ingresado por la sección, el Barça de baloncesto destinó alrededor de 1,48 euros a gastos de personal.

articles.title: The predominant basketball dynasty on Earth is at stake as America's eyes turn to Caitlin Clark's role
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's bench role is under scrutiny as Team USA enters the FIBA Women's World Cup knockout stage with its 33-game winning streak at stake.
articles.body: American dominance is on the line in this second week of September. The U.S. women's basketball team is among the predominant dynasties in modern international sports, and have won eight consecutive Olympic gold medals and four consecutive World Cups. They have not lost a game at either event since 2006, and three victories in Berlin have extended their World Cup winning streak to 33 games. Their Olympic win streak is at 61 games. The U.S. has never lost a quarterfinal game in the FIBA Women's World Cup, and they will look to keep that going on Thursday. But they will have to do it with their biggest star in an undefined role. CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK Caitlin Clark has come off the bench in all three group stage games for the US. She went from a record-setting 14-point, 11-assist debut against China to scoring just one point and missing every field goal in a career-low game against Italy, as the U.S. nearly suffered a devastating upset. Clark rebounded with nine points and seven assists in a blowout win against Czechia to close the group stage. But going into the knockout stage, as France and Belgium have looked more dominant than the U.S., Clark's role will be a subject of higher consequence, both on the court and on social media. Many fans have called for other young stars like Paige Buecker and Angel Reese to start as well. And as America will look to defend its Olympic dynasty in home soil in 2028, what happens with Clark, Bueckers and Reese in this next week will be the world's last impression of how those three gel until LA28. What has been done with Clark so far? Clark's chemistry with her World Cup teammates was on display in a viral video where three other players appeared to point and laugh as she bent her bare feet backward under a bench to hide them from a camera in the locker room. The players laughing included Reese and Fever teammate Aliyah Boston. Team USA Coach Kara Lawson has used Clark as a change-of-pace guard off the bench. That strategy looked nearly perfect in the opener against China. Clark entered the game and immediately accelerated the American offense. She finished with 14 points and 11 assists in 25 minutes as the U.S. won 94-61. She did not commit a turnover. Her 11 assists were the most ever by an American in a Women’s World Cup debut. Clark also became the first player from any country to record at least 10 assists without a turnover in a World Cup game since FIBA began tracking the statistic in 1994. CAITLIN CLARK VS PAIGE BUECKERS: HOW TWO WHITE WNBA STARS WOUND UP WITH VASTLY DIFFERENT CULTURAL PERCEPTIONS Clark said that she was prepared to accept a different role than the one she holds with the Indiana Fever after the China game "Being surrounded by five people who have won gold medals before at the highest level, I try to follow their lead and take every bit of wisdom they try to give me," Clark said, according to FIBA. Lawson kept Clark on the bench against Italy, but with more frustrating and frightening results for Americans. Clark played 19 minutes and missed all six of her field-goal attempts. She finished with one point and one assist while committing two turnovers. It marked the first time in her college or WNBA career that she failed to make a field goal. Lawson then kept Clark on the bench for the final seven minutes. The U.S. relied on its veteran guards as it erased a late deficit and escaped with a 55-52 victory. The Americans shot 29% and made only two of their 24 attempts from 3-point range. Their 55 points were their fewest in a World Cup game since FIBA introduced the 3-point line in 1984, according to FIBA. Clark responded against Czechia one day later. She recorded nine points and seven assists off the bench in a 105-64 victory that secured first place in Group D. Through three games, Clark has produced 24 points and 19 assists. That decision will carry more weight from this point forward, with higher stakes and tougher competition in the final round. If the U.S. falls behind late in the quarterfinals, Lawson will have to decide whether to protect the dynasty with the veterans who built it or place the ball in the hands of the player expected to lead its next generation. What about Reese and Bueckers? Bueckers and Reese have also come off the bench alongside Clark in every game. The three stars have already spent years colliding in games that helped transform women’s basketball. Clark and Bueckers were teammates on the United States’ 2019 U19 gold-medal team before splitting two NCAA Tournament meetings. UConn won their 2021 Sweet 16 matchup, but Iowa answered with a 71-69 victory in the 2024 Final Four—a game that drew 14.2 million viewers. Clark and Reese produced the more heated rivalry. Reese helped LSU defeat Clark and Iowa in the 2023 national championship, then celebrated with a hand gesture that sparked a nationwide debate about sportsmanship, race and double standards. Clark got her revenge in the 2024 Elite Eight, recording 41 points and 12 assists as Iowa defeated LSU despite Reese’s 17 points and 20 rebounds. Reese left college with LSU’s 2023 national title, while Bueckers won her championship with UConn in 2025. Clark never captured the trophy, but she reached consecutive championship games and helped drive the sport to record television audiences. Now the three players who became famous under the brightest lights are trying to win together—and doing so from Team USA’s bench. So far in the World Cup, Bueckers has been a more consistent scorer than Clark. She matched Clark with 14 points in the opener against China and added four assists and two steals. She then produced one of the strongest all-around performances for the U.S. during its scare against Italy. Bueckers finished with seven points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks in 19 minutes. She also made the Americans’ first 3-pointer after the team missed its first 10 attempts. Bueckers followed that performance with 10 points and five assists against Czechia. She has made 13 of her 22 field-goal attempts through three games while committing only three turnovers. Meanwhile, Reese collected nine rebounds in 17 minutes against China, including five on the offensive glass. That effort became especially valuable against a Chinese roster built around one of the tallest frontcourts in the tournament. Reese then made her biggest impact when the rest of the American offense struggled against Italy. She scored eight points in 15 minutes, made all four of her free throws and recorded two blocks. Reese added 13 points and six rebounds in the victory over Czechia. Through three games, she has produced 26 points and 18 rebounds despite playing fewer than 20 minutes in each appearance. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! America's greatest threats The U.S. earned a direct trip to the quarterfinals by winning Group D. It will face the winner of Hungary and Japan on Thursday. Neither team would enter that game as a favorite. Hungary has not reached the World Cup quarterfinals in 40 years, while Japan has not made it that far since 1979. But the Americans’ three-point escape against Italy showed how quickly a heavy favorite can find itself in danger during a single-elimination game. The road could become much harder in the semifinals. The U.S. would face Spain or the winner of the qualifying game between Italy and Australia. Italy has already shown it can threaten the Americans. The Italians held the U.S. to 55 points—its lowest total in a major international tournament in decades—and had a chance to tie the game in the final seconds. Australia has reached the podium at each of the last three World Cups. Spain finished second at the 2025 European championship and opened this tournament by beating host Germany by 30 points. However, Spain also suffered one of the tournament’s biggest upsets when it lost to Mali during group play. The two most serious threats sit on the other side of the bracket. France looked like the tournament’s most dominant team during the opening round. The French went 3-0 and outscored their opponents 305-178. They defeated Hungary by 46 points, Korea by 26 and Nigeria by 55. France also made a World Cup-record 22 three-pointers against Nigeria. A potential U.S.-France championship game would carry recent history. France came within one point of ending the American Olympic dynasty in the 2024 gold-medal game. Gabby Williams made a shot at the buzzer, but her foot was inside the three-point line, allowing the U.S. to escape with a 67-66 victory. Belgium may present an equally difficult challenge. The Belgians also finished group play 3-0 and closed it with an 80-68 victory over Australia. Emma Meesseman recorded 22 points and 10 rebounds in that game, while Julie Allemand became the World Cup’s all-time assists leader. Belgium has also won consecutive European championships. It defeated Spain in the 2023 and 2025 finals, including a dramatic 14-0 closing run to erase a 12-point deficit in the final minutes of last year’s title game. France and Belgium are positioned to meet in the semifinals, meaning the U.S. could face only one of them in the championship game. That may be the best news the Americans received from the bracket. The U.S. still has the deepest collection of talent in Berlin. But France has been more dominant, Belgium has more continuity and Italy has already exposed how vulnerable the Americans can look on a poor shooting night. Three more victories would preserve the dynasty. articles.title: Former Hendricken star throws rare Triple-A perfect game in win
articles.summary: Pannone is in the midst of his second stint with the Milwaukee Brewers organization and started in the big leagues vs. San Francisco in July.
articles.body:
Thomas Pannone certainly made the most of having to work on Labor Day.

The former Bishop Hendricken baseball standout fired a perfect game for Triple-A Nashville in a 3-0 win at Durham. The left-hander's superb performance Monday evening, Sept, 7, was the first such nine-inning effort in the minor leagues since 2017 and just the fifth in the 142-year history of the International League.

Pannone threw 61 of his 94 pitches for strikes, capping his gem at Durham Bulls Athletic Park in North Carolina by inducing a Homer Bush Jr. bouncer to shortstop. Eduardo Garcia fielded coming in and threw across to first baseman Blake Burke for the 27 th and final out of the evening. Pannone was rushed by his teammates at the center of the diamond and applauded by the road crowd of 6,637 fans.

Pannone struggled to find his command early, falling behind each of the game's first two hitters and going to a quick 3-0 count against Carson Williams leading off the bottom of the second. Williams decided to be aggressive and swung at the next two pitchers, fouling off a borderline four-seam fastball before lining to center.

Pannone settled into a rhythm from there, cruising into the bottom of the ninth before going to 2-0 for just the second time since the early innings against Blake Sabol. Two foul balls and a grounder to Garcia at short put Pannone two outs away, and Logan Davidson followed by lining a first-pitch sinker to left. Bush jumped ahead 3-0 while standing between Pannone and history before taking a called strike and rolling over a sinker on the outside corner.

The Sounds plated single runs in the three different innings to back Pannone. Garcia lined an RBI single to left in the third and Ramon Rodriguez sent a run-scoring double to left in the fourth. Garcia added a long solo homer to left in the eighth, a 421-foot blast to highlight his 2-for-4 night at the plate.

Pannone allowed 15 hits over his last three starts in August, covering just 8 2/3 innings. He threw four scoreless frames against Louisville last time out, reaching five strikeouts for the fifth time this season. The eight strikeouts Pannone posted in this outing were his most in a Triple-A game since fanning nine with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in August 2024.

Pannone is in the midst of his second stint with the Milwaukee Brewers organization and made a start in the big leagues against the San Francisco Giants in late July. His pair of strikeouts against former Boston Red Sox slugger Rafael Devers were a personal highlight in a loss at Oracle Park, a first time out in the majors for Pannone since 2023. He debuted with the Toronto Blue Jays in 2018 and has also spent parts of two years with the Kia Tigers in the KBO League.

Pannone missed all of 2025 recovering from a torn left flexor tendon. He returned with three scoreless innings in an April outing against Worcester and started for the 20 th time this season on Monday. The 32-year-old collected his 300 th professional appearance last time out against the Bats.

Pannone also starred in the outfield while winning three state championships with the Hawks in 2009, 2010 and 2012. He made an initial commitment to Miami before enrolling instead with the College of Southern Nevada to speed up his draft clock. Pannone was selected in the ninth round by the Cleveland Guardians in 2013, signed for $120,000 and was part of a July 2017 trade with Toronto for relief pitcher Joe Smith that helped clear a path to the top.

Pannone joins an exclusive pitching club that includes a local tie. Pawtucket Red Sox right-hander Tomo Ohka fired a perfect game at McCoy Stadium in June 2000, a 76-pitch blanking of the Charlotte Knights. Ohka etched his own name into both PawSox and minor league history on that night.

articles.title: After 67 years, major quarter horse racing event moving to Texas
articles.summary: The big purse events have been around since 1959.
articles.body:
While it isn't quite the widely known troika of the Kentucky Derby , Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes, another major horse racing triple crown is moving to Texas, leaving its old home for the first time in nearly seven decades.

Johnny and Jana Trotter, owners of Ruidoso Downs in Ruidoso, N.M., agreed on a tentative deal with Global Gaming Solutions to move multiple quarter horse racing events and assets, including each race in its annual Triple Crown Series, to Lone Star Park in Grand Prairie, about 20 miles west of Dallas. The move, announced Sept. 3 , would go into effect in 2027.

What's moving to Texas include the three quarter horse Triple Crown Futurity races: the $1 million Ruidoso Futurity, the $1 million Rainbow Futurity and $3 million All-American Futurity, plus the All-American Super Select Sale and the Ruidoso Downs Hall of Fame. The triple crown races are the richest in quarter horse racing . The Hall of Fame includes an annual induction event.

The move comes after major challenges for Ruidoso Downs. Floods damaged the facility in 2024, prompting the American Quarter Horse Association (AQHA) to temporarily relocate the All American Futurity to the New Mexico State Fare in Albuquerque. Unfortunately, floods once again prompted its move to Albuquerque in '25. This summer, a house fire impacted the area of Ruidoso Downs. The All-American race which dates to 1959, stayed in Albuquerque for 2026. It was run Monday.

"Following the fires and floods of recent years, we have taken a hard look at what comes next and evaluated every realistic path forward," read a statement by Ruidoso Downs General Manager Rick Baugh in the Sept. 3 announcement. "Our responsibility has always been to protect not just a place but a legacy."

Lone Star Park opened in 1997 in Grand Prairie, covering 315 acres with accommodations for 1,600 horses. Global Gaming Solutions, which is based within the Chickasaw Nation in Oklahoma, also operates Remington Park in Oklahoma City and multiple casinos.

"The All-American Triple Crown Series, Super Select Sale and Hall of Fame have a treasured history among owners, trainers, jockeys and the countless racing fans who love the horse racing experience," read a statement in the announcement by Global Gaming Solutions CEO Skip Seeley. "We are excited about the opportunity to continue these storied traditions at Lone Star Park and introduce them to racing fans across North Texas and beyond."

articles.title: “I think we’re going to be in for some fun surprises”: Ayesha Curry boldly predicts Stephen Curry’s upcoming season with Warriors
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry is heading into a season with high championship expectations. A knee injury wiped out much of his 2025-26 campaign, and now, with a new .
articles.body: Stephen Curry is heading into a season with high championship expectations. A knee injury wiped out much of his 2025-26 campaign, and now, with a new contract on the table, Golden State's franchise cornerstone is being asked two questions at once: can he stay healthy, and will he stay a Warrior for good?His wife, Ayesha Curry, isn't worried about either one. Ayesha recently offered a glimpse into what she's seeing behind the scenes, and it's the kind of comment that gets Warriors fans talking before training camp even opens.Ayesha Curry makes bold Stephen Curry prediction for upcoming seasonStephen Curry's 2025-26 season never really found its footing. Runner's knee kept him out for stretches, and he finished with just 43 regular-season appearances, one of the lowest totals of his career outside of the shortened 2019-20 and 2011-12 seasons. Golden State finished 37-45, and the flashes of vintage Curry, like his outburst in the play-in game in Los Angeles, couldn't carry over into the next round against Phoenix.Ayesha's comments to NBC Sports Bay Area revealed a subtle picture. She described her husband as someone who hasn't taken a break since the season ended, training with the same intensity that's defined his career. “Steph is the hardest-working man in the room. He has no days off. He hasn’t stopped since last season ended. He’s ready. He’s ready to get out there,” she said, before adding that the next coming years could bring some genuinely surprising moments for Golden State. “I think we’re going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years.”Ayesha is confident in her prediction as Steph gears up for the upcoming season.Stephen Curry spills the beans on contract situation with WarriorsCurry became eligible for a new maximum extension over the weekend, right as he begins preparing for his 18th NBA season. He's currently under contract through 2026-27 at $62.6 million, the highest annual salary in the league, and the NBA's Over-38 Rule caps any new deal at two years and $136.7 million.Despite the number crunching swirling around him, Curry made his stance clear during an event for his and Ayesha's Eat. Learn. Play. foundation. "There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career," he told NBC Sports Bay Area, brushing aside any suggestion that his future lies elsewhere.He also made a point of separating the business side from basketball. Contract talks, he explained, won't distract him or the team from preparing for a season he badly wants to make count, especially after watching so much of last year from the sidelines. At 38, with 26.6 points per game and a 12th All-Star selection to show for an injury-shortened year, Curry isn't chasing validation. He's chasing a healthy season, and by his own account, and his wife's, he's already put in the work to get there.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 76ers, Flyers Post Rendering Photos of Spectrum-Inspired Arena Scheduled to Open in 2030
articles.summary: The NBA's Philadelphia 76ers and NHL's Philadelphia Flyers shared artist renderings Tuesday of their upcoming new arena.
articles.body:
The NBA's Philadelphia 76ers and NHL's Philadelphia Flyers shared artist renderings Tuesday of their upcoming new arena.

ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania posted some of the images on X, showcasing what is currently being called Philadelphia Arena:

Per Charania and ESPN's Emily Kaplan , the arena is planned to open before the 2030 WNBA season, which is when Philadelphia's expansion team will begin play.

The arena will be built at the site of The Spectrum in South Philly. The Spectrum was home to both the Sixers and Flyers from 1967 to 1996, and it hosted the AHL's Philadelphia Phantoms from 1996 to 2009 as well.

In 1996, the 76ers and Flyers made the move to Xfinity Mobile Arena, which was previously known as the CoreStates Center, First Union Center, Wachovia Center and Wells Fargo Center.

The design of the new arena is undoubtedly inspired by The Spectrum, but it will have a modern twist.

Comcast Spectacor and the 76ers are partnering to make the new venue a reality, and Sixers managing partner Josh Harris expressed excitement over the project in a statement, saying, "Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that. This privately funded arena will be the home to moments and memories that define this city for generations."

The Flyers and 76ers are in the midst of two of the longest championship droughts in their respective leagues, and they are undoubtedly hopeful that the new arena will bring good fortune.

The Flyers have not won a Stanley Cup since winning it in back-to-back years in 1974 and 1975, while the 76ers last won an NBA title in 1983.

Things are looking up for both franchises, though, as the Flyers ended a five-year playoff drought last season, while the Sixers established themselves as championship contenders this offseason by acquiring Jaylen Brown and signing LeBron James.

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers get another exciting news after landing Lebron James ahead of 2026-27 season that could fuel $6 billion economic growth
articles.summary: NBA News: Philadelphia 76ers’ basketball future just got a lot more interesting. And of course, it's not only because of what's happening on the roster. LeBron .
articles.body: Philadelphia 76ers’ basketball future just got a lot more interesting. And of course, it's not only because of what's happening on the roster. LeBron James is joining the 76ers for his 24th NBA season, a move that on its own would dominate headlines around the league. But the Sixers organization has more going on right now than one blockbuster signing.Across town, the plans for a new home for both the 76ers and the Flyers are finally taking shape, with a timeline that give Philadelphia sports fans plenty to think about heading into the new year.Philadelphia 76ers and Flyers get major arena update ahead of 2030 openingThe 76ers and Flyers have released renderings for a new arena on the old Spectrum site in South Philadelphia, and the organizations are billing it as the largest privately funded project the city has ever seen. It's set to open before the 2030 WNBA season, timed to coincide with the debut of Philadelphia's incoming expansion franchise. After more than a decade as tenants, the Sixers are stepping into a 50-50 ownership partnership with Comcast Spectator for the new building.Comcast chairman Brian Roberts framed the project as a turning point for the city. "This is a new era for Philadelphia sports," he said (via ESPN), pointing to the site's history with Ed Snider and the original Spectrum as part of what makes the location meaningful. The design leans into that legacy too, with more than half an acre of outdoor space, food and beverage areas, and a grand staircase modeled after the steps outside the Philadelphia Museum of Art.Sixers managing partner Josh Harris shared that Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world and that this privately funded project will host moments fans remember for generations. "Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that," he shared. For the Flyers, there's a symbolism, since the move returns the franchise to the ground where it began play in 1967 and won both of its Stanley Cups.NHL commissioner Gary Bettman also weighed in, calling it a state-of-the-art home worthy of the team and describing the investment as a vote of confidence in Philadelphia's long-term future. All told, the project is projected to create close to 15,000 jobs and generate nearly $6 billion in economic activity over the next decade.Philadelphia 76ers entering new season with a revamped rosterLeBron James is reportedly taking a significant pay cut to make the move work, agreeing to a two-year deal worth around $8 million with a player option, a steep drop from the more than $50 million he made last season with the Lakers. At 41, he's not chasing another big paycheck. He's chasing a title in a city that hasn't celebrated one since 1983.He'll slot into a roster already built around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, with Jaylen Brown and veteran guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope adding experience on both ends of the floor. Younger pieces like rookie guard VJ Edgecombe give the roster some long-term upside alongside the win-now additions. It's an unusual mix of aging stars and rising talent, and how head coach Nick Nurse blends the two will likely define whether this version of the Sixers becomes a real contender or just an interesting experiment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Barça presenta su revolución: 11 fichajes para acabar con tres años en blanco
articles.standfirst: Nkamhoua, Evbuomwan, Ubal, Martin, Robinson, Umude, Balcerowski, Gibson, Nebo, Minaya y Makoundou, además del entrenador Aleksander Sekulic, son las caras nuevas del proyecto
articles.summary: Los azulgranas
articles.body: La revolución que el Barcelona emprendió al final de la pasada temporada se presentó este martes. Las 11 incorporaciones posaron con sus respectivas camisetas. En la parte posterior de las mismas, nombres lejos del estrellato en un proyecto arriesgado: Olivier Nkamhoua, Tosan Evbuomwan, Agustín Ubal, Tyrese Martin, Justin Robinson, Stanley Umude, Olek Balcerowski, Umoja Gibson, Josh Nebo, Justin Minaya y Yoan Makoundou. Todos ellos, a las órdenes de Aleksander Sekulic, que también se estrena en el banquillo del Palau. El objetivo, pese a lo novedoso del proyecto, es volver a ganar a títulos y acabar con la pésima racha de tres temporadas consecutivas en blanco, algo que no pasaba desde hacía 48 años. "Cuando pienso en jugar con el Barça lo único que me viene a la mente es ganar. Este club tiene una cultura ganadora", dijo Martin. "El objetivo es volver a ganar títulos”, confesó Robinson. "Los 11 nuevos jugadores responden a un perfil atlético, con piernas frescas, buena mentalidad y muchas ganas de crecer", valora Xevi Pujol, otra novedad, aunque en los despachos como nuevo director deportivo del baloncesto azulgrana. Sólo permanecen cuatro integrantes de la plantilla del curso pasado: Kevin Punter, Joel Parra, Darío Brizuela y Juan Núñez. Se han marchado Willy Hernangómez, Tomas Satoransky, Nico Laprovittola, Will Clyburn, Toko Shengelia, Youssoupha Fall, Juani Marcos, Myles Cale y Miles Norris mientras que Jan Vesely anunció su retirada. Algunos de ellos, dada su edad, probablemente ya habían ofrecido el mejor baloncesto de sus carreras y su físico tampoco era el mejor. Las 10 salidas tenían una media de 31,8 años y las 11 llegadas promedian 26,1, casi 5,7 años menos. En contraposición de esa ganancia de físico y piernas, el equipo pierde mucha experiencia. De las 11 incorporaciones, hay seis jugadores que nunca han disputado la Euroliga y algunos vivirán sus primeras aventuras en Europa, lo que siempre conlleva un riesgo en cuanto a la adaptación. "Hemos priorizado un perfil por encima de las posiciones tradicionales. Hemos encontrado un equilibrio entre personalidad y características que nos puede hacer crecer", explica Pujol, que llega procendente del Kosner Baskonia, donde apenas le han permitido trabajar una temporada tras confirmarse como un gran conocedor del mercado en su etapa en Manresa. Pujol cree que "el primer gran reto, después de la pretemporada, es seguir trabajando desde la competición oficial, para construir el grupo, desarrollarse tácticamente e ir asumiendo el estilo de juego que queremos". El próximo sábado 19 de septiembre, los azulgranas disputarán la semifinal de la Supercopa Endesa ante el Valencia Basket, primer partido oficial y reedición de la final de la Liga Endesa de la campaña pasada. El Barcelona, con las marchas de algunos pesos pesados, también ha aligerado su masa salarial. La temporada pasada, según cifras ofrecidas por 2Playbook, la sección de baloncesto redujo un 7,1% su cifra de negocio, hasta 19,5 millones de euros. Pese a ello, redujo sus pérdidas un 13,9%, hasta 17,7 millones de euros, gracias a que redujo su masa salarial, que es donde se encuentra el principal factor de presión en sus cuentas. El club blaugrana destinó 28,9 millones de euros a salarios, casi 3 millones menos que en la temporada 2024-2025.
