articles.title: Grizzlies, Pelicans Reportedly Swap Former 1st-Round NBA Draft Picks in Trade Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Needing to clear money to complete their signing of Bennedict Mathurin, the New Orleans Pelicans are trading Jordan Hawkins and Micah Peavy to the Memphis Grizzlies in a four-player deal.
articles.body:
Needing to clear money to complete their signing of Bennedict Mathurin, the New Orleans Pelicans are trading Jordan Hawkins and Micah Peavy to the Memphis Grizzlies in a four-player deal.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania , Hawkins and Peavy will go to Memphis with AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson coming back to New Orleans.

The Grizzlies will also receive a future second-round pick and a second-round pick swap in the trade.

ESPN's Bobby Marks added the deal saves $5.7 million for the Pelicans, who recently agreed to a two-year, $16 million contract with Mathurin.

Per Spotrac's Keith Smith , the Pelicans are now roughly $7.9 million under the tax after the trade before factoring in Mathurin's contract that will hard cap them at the first apron.

In addition to the financial maneuvering of the trade, it's also something of a challenge deal involving two recent first-round draft picks who have not panned out thus far.

Johnson, the No. 23 pick in the 2024 draft, is already on his fourth different team. He started his NBA career with the Milwaukee Bucks, then was traded to the Washington Wizards midway through his rookie year in the Khris Middleton deal.

Washington sent Johnson to the Dallas Mavericks last season prior to the trade deadline in February, then he was traded to Memphis in July as part of a six-team deal involving 11 players.

Johnson has averaged 4.9 points in 77 appearances with three different clubs over the past two years.

Hawkins was originally drafted with the No. 14 pick by the Pelicans in 2023. He has appeared in 174 games over the past three seasons, averaging a career-high 10.8 points during the 2024-25 campaign.

Peavy, the 40th overall pick in the 2025 draft, played 61 games for the Wizards as a rookie. Gibson, who turned 41 on June 24, is the second-oldest active NBA player after LeBron James.

articles.title: Lakers' Jarred Vanderbilt Drops Video Showcasing Luka Doncic, Team's Minicamp in Slovenia
articles.summary: In the wake of the Los Angeles Lakers' minicamp in Slovenia hosted by Luka Dončić, Jarred Vanderbilt has provided some insights into the trip.
articles.body:
In the wake of the Los Angeles Lakers' minicamp in Slovenia hosted by Luka Dončić, Jarred Vanderbilt has provided some insights into the trip.

Vanderbilt posted a video on his Instagram documenting the team's journey that included meeting fans, playing golf, sight-seeing and swimming.

Dončić, who is from Slovenia, reportedly chartered a plane for 14 members of the Lakers. They also received gift bags, were treated to a meal at Dončić's favorite restaurant and went fishing at Lake Bled.

The trip lasted for five days and was intended to be a team-bonding exercise for a Lakers squad that has undergone significant changes in the offseason, including a surprise agreement by Mark Walter to sell the franchise just 10 months after his purchase was approved by the NBA board of governors.

LeBron James' departure left no doubt that Dončić is the face of the franchise now and into the future. The Lakers also signed Austin Reaves to a four-year, $185 million contract and gave Walker Kessler a four-year, $130 million deal in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz.

Time will tell if those big investments pay off for the Lakers, but Dončić took the initiative this summer to make sure this team can be as closely bonded as possible going into the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Pelicans send former first-round pick Jordan Hawkins to Grizzlies to free up space for Bennedict Mathurin
articles.summary: The Pelicans needed to free up cap space to sign Bennedict Mathurin.
articles.body:
Jordan Hawkins hasn't blossomed into the star the New Orleans Pelicans expected when the team selected him in the first round of the 2023 NBA Draft. Because of that, the Pelicans reportedly felt comfortable moving on from Hawkins on Tuesday, shipping him and Micah Peavy to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, according to ESPN.

The Pelicans are also sending a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Grizzlies in the deal, per ESPN.

While it's not a major deal on the surface, the Pelicans had a reason for making it. With the move, the Pelicans saved $5.7 million, giving them the necessary cap space to sign Bennedict Mathurin, per ESPN's Bobby Marks. While news broke in August that the Pelicans were signing Mathurin to a two-year deal , the team still needed to make room for the veteran. Trading away Hawkins and Peavy made that possible.

Since being selected as the No. 14 overall pick in 2023, Hawkins failed to develop into a consistent starter with the Pelicans. He's started just 20 of the 174 games he's played with the franchise since the draft.

Hawkins, 24, showed promise during the 2024-25 NBA season, averaging 10.8 points in 56 games, but saw that figure drop to just 5.1 points per game last season. He has one more year left on his rookie contract.

Peavy, 25, averaged 4.3 points per game as a rookie with the Pelicans.

Johnson, 21, is another first-round pick who has yet to break out in the NBA. Despite his age, Johnson has now been traded three times. He'll look for some stability with the Grizzlies. Johnson averaged 3.3 points last season.

At 41, Gibson is the odd man out in the deal, by age, at least. The 17-year veteran is looking to make it one more year in the NBA. Over the past seven seasons or so, Gibson has filled a bench role with a number of different teams. He is capable of putting up a few points and pulling down a few rebounds in limited work.

articles.title: 76ers Felt They Were 'Long Shot' in Jaylen Brown Trade Sweepstakes, New NBA Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers reportedly doubted their ability to trade for a key piece of their bid to sign LeBron James before all the pieces fell into place earlier this offseason.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers reportedly doubted their ability to trade for a key piece of their bid to sign LeBron James before all the pieces fell into place earlier this offseason.

The Sixers saw themselves as a "long shot" to acquire Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics before finalizing a trade for him in July, The Athletic's Tony Jones reported Tuesday.

Brown then reportedly played a role in recruiting James to sign a two-year deal with the Sixers later that month.

According to Jones, there was a change in dynamics surrounding Brown's availability when reports surfaced the Celtics had put him on the trade block in a failed bid for former Milwaukee Bucks star Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Even with those reports seemingly putting pressure on the Celtics to move on from Brown, Jones reported the Sixers saw themselves as an underdog in part because "conventional wisdom" suggested the Western Conference as a more likely landing spot than within the division.

The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski recently reported on CLNS' Celtics Daily the Minnesota Timberwolves had "real discussions" with the Celtics about a potential Brown trade earlier this offseason.

The Wolves instead finalized a deal with the Charlotte Hornets for LaMelo Ball while the Sixers agreed to send Brown to a division rival in exchange for Paul George and four draft picks, including a pair of first-rounders.

Krawczynski reported the Wolves had found the Celtics' asking price for Brown too high and that the team was "happy with the LaMelo fit a little bit more than they would have been with the Jaylen fit."

Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens said after the Brown trade his team had agreed to the deal because the Sixers' first-rounders represented "two potential premium assets."

Brown is now preparing to make his regular-season Sixers debut Oct. 20 at the New York Knicks before reuniting with Jayson Tatum and the rest of his former teammates in a Nov. 10 matchup against the visiting Celtics.

articles.title: La otra victoria del Mundial: Una canasta para cambiar vidas
articles.standfirst: Más de 400 niños y niñas en una iniciativa de la Fundación FIBA con Basketball For Good y el baloncesto como herramienta de inclusión, educación y transformación social.
articles.summary: Más de 400 niños y niñas en una iniciativa de la Fundación FIBA con Basketball For Good y el baloncesto como herramienta de inclusión, educación y transformación social.
articles.body: El Mundial femenino de FIBA que se disputa en Berlín está dejando espectáculo dentro de la pista y también historias que trascienden el marcador. Mientras las mejores selecciones del planeta pelean por las medallas, más de 400 niños y niñas han vivido su particular Mundial gracias a Little Champions, una iniciativa de la FIBA Foundation integrada en el programa Basketball For Good. Antes de cada partido, comparten unos minutos con las estrellas, salen a la pista junto a ellas, reciben sus sonrisas, sus palabras y sus choques de manos. Para muchos, un recuerdo para toda la vida. Las imágenes de Iyana Martín charlando con una de las niñas o de Alicia Florez compartiendo confidencias antes de los partidos de España reflejan el verdadero valor de esos momentos. Son escenas sencillas, pero cargadas de significado: niños que hasta hace poco veían a sus referentes desde la grada ahora caminan junto a ellos por la misma pista. Y las jugadoras, que algún día ocuparon ese mismo lugar como aficionadas, tienen la oportunidad de convertirse en inspiración para una nueva generación. Porque el objetivo de Basketball For Good va mucho más allá de acercar a los niños a un gran campeonato. La FIBA Foundation utiliza el baloncesto como una herramienta de transformación social, con tres grandes pilares: liderazgo juvenil, minibasket e impacto comunitario. Los resultados dan dimensión al proyecto: en 2025 sus iniciativas alcanzaron a más de 376.000 jóvenes y líderes comunitarios en 127 países, mientras más de 830 agentes de cambio recibieron apoyo. En Rwanda, el baloncesto sirve para impulsar la igualdad y el liderazgo entre niñas; en el campo de refugiados de Kakuma, en Kenia, para ofrecer a los jóvenes un espacio de convivencia y aprendizaje; y en Bhutan, para acercar el deporte a niños sordos y con dificultades auditivas. La Fundación apuesta además por que los propios protagonistas sean quienes impulsen el cambio. Su programa Propose a Project recibió 332 solicitudes en 2025 y permitió financiar 73 proyectos de base con más de 100.000 dólares. La idea es que sean las propias comunidades quienes identifiquen sus necesidades y encuentren en el baloncesto una vía para combatir problemas como la desigualdad, la exclusión, la falta de oportunidades o los hábitos poco saludables. Un modelo que en 2026 mantiene su crecimiento y amplía el interés por una iniciativa que pretende que el impacto del baloncesto no termine cuando suena la bocina. Los Youth Leaders completan ese círculo. La FIBA Foundation forma a jóvenes para que puedan convertirse después en líderes, entrenadores, mentores o impulsores de nuevos proyectos en sus comunidades. En 2025 también llevó su mensaje a los grandes campeonatos, con 21 activaciones vinculadas a competiciones continentales y torneos de formación. El propósito es que cada gran evento deje algo más que un campeón, unas estadísticas o una audiencia millonaria: que también genere un legado social allí donde se celebra. Por eso los niños que estos días saltan a la pista de Berlín junto a las jugadoras son mucho más que una imagen bonita antes de un partido. Son la expresión más visible de una filosofía que pretende demostrar que el baloncesto puede cambiar vidas. Quizá alguno descubra su pasión por este deporte; quizá una niña gane confianza, un joven encuentre su vocación de liderazgo o una cancha se convierta en punto de encuentro para una comunidad. En un Mundial repleto de triples, rebotes y canastas decisivas, hay una victoria que no aparece en el marcador. Es conseguir que alguien se sienta parte del juego. Esa es la otra victoria del Mundial. La canasta más solidaria de la Fundación FIBA.

articles.standfirst: El entrenador, que dirige a los Liaoning Flying Leopards en la CBA de China, fue acusado de participar en la trama de la tramitación de los pasaportes falsos de Slaughter y Panko
articles.summary: El entrenador, que dirige a los Liaoning Flying Leopards en la CBA de China, fue acusado de participar en la trama de la tramitación de los pasaportes falsos de Slaughter y Panko
articles.body: El 'Caso Panko' sacudió el baloncesto español hace unos años. El asunto que vio la luz en 2016 tenía todos los ingredientes de una serie de televisión: pasaportes falsos de dudosa procedencia, una dictadura africana, un error burdo y algunos intermediarios interesados en el negocio. Los nombres más reconocibles de la trama fueron los exjugadores Andy Panko y Marcus Slaughter, que militó en el Real Madrid. Pero también aparecían implicados, el representante de ambos, Julián Aranda, un mediador con contactos en Guinea Ecuatorial, el exjugador Richard Nguema, que a su vez conocía al técnico Hugo López. El entrenador pucelano dirigía por aquel entonces a los Malabo Kings. El error de bulto en la tramitación falsa del pasaporte 'cotonou' (los dos documentos tenían la misma numeración) llamó la atención de la FEB y el CSD. Ahora, el proceso judicial que se inició tras la denuncia ha terminado, de momento, con la condena por falsedad documental de Panko, Aranda y Nguema y la absolución completa de Hugo López. Para el entrenador pucelano, ‘vetado’ por la ACB desde su primer experiencia al frente de un equipo (Fuenlabrada, 2014-2015) tras su exitosa trayectoria como técnico ayudante de Pablo Laso en el Real Madrid, la sentencia supone un alivio absoluto y la confirmación de lo que él mantuvo desde el inicio del proceso: era inocente al 100 por 100. Atrás queda un capítulo muy amargo en su trayectoria profesional y personal, una historia chabacana que le ocasionó, casi por accidente, un enorme daño reputacional. Se despeja cualquier tipo de duda sobre su comportamiento en relación a los hechos. “A Hugo López se le declara absuelto de los delitos que se le imputan al considerar que no existe suficiente prueba en su contra más allá de indicios que se resumen en la facilitación del teléfono de Nguema, hablar por teléfono con Aranda y una nueva conversación posterior, siendo merecedor de ello en base al principio in dubio pro reo”. Así reza la sentencia judicial. Panko y Aranda han sido condenados a cinco meses de prisión y para Nguema la pena es de 10 meses. Todos se enfrentaban a cargos de prisión que llegaban hasta casi los dos años. Después de aquel escándalo que le salpicó únicamente por dar un número de teléfono, la carrera de Hugo dio un giro. La ACB se 'olvidó' del entrenador pucelano. Y como se dice en el argot, ‘se salió de la rueda’, pero no voluntariamente. Su carrera, sin embargo, no ha dejado de ser exitosa: ganó el triplete de títulos en Angola, conquistó la Liga China y la Liga de Canadá con el Halifax, fue entrenador de año en la LEB Oro con el Valladolid y ha sido seleccionador de Suecia durante tres temporadas. Un entrenador de verdad que nunca falsificó nada.

articles.title: Why Trae Young-Zach LaVine Trade Was Turned Down by Kings Revealed in New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings reportedly passed on a chance to trade Zach LaVine for Trae Young.
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings reportedly passed on a chance to trade Zach LaVine for Trae Young.

ESPN 1320 Sacramento's James Ham said on Monday's episode of the Locked on Kings podcast the Kings declined the potential deal for Young, who was traded from the Atlanta Hawks to Washington Wizards in January.

"According to a source of mine, they said no because they knew the second he got off the plane he would want an extension, and the Kings were not fully prepared to be in the long-term Trae business," Ham said around the 4:00 mark of the podcast.

Ham continued, "They have their own agenda here, and it did not include bringing in Trae Young on a potential $250, $300 million extension."

Young agreed in June to a four-year, $212 million deal that is set to keep him in Washington, D.C. through at least 2028-29 with a player option for his age-31 campaign in 2029-30.

The Kings only have LaVine under contract for one more season after he opted in to his $49 million option for the 2026-27 campaign.

Dealing with LaVine's expiring deal rather than Young's new extension will give Kings general manager Scott Perry more flexibility to navigate the franchise's future either with or without Domantas Sabonis.

ESPN's Anthony Slater recently reported the Kings have previously discussed trades for Sabonis and "aren't interested" in discussing an extension past the 2028 expiration of the big man's current contract.

With De'Andre Hunter also heading into next season on an expiring contract, Perry could look to give the Kings a fresh start ahead of next season by potentially moving on from Hunter and LaVine while considering a possible Sabonis trade .

articles.title: How Orioles’ September call-up can capitalize on Luis Robert Jr.’s injury
articles.summary: This is a big moment for the Orioles outfielder.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles are fading further away from the American League Wild Card race.

The AL East club is 4-6 in its last 10 games and needs a strong finish to overtake the Texas Rangers , Toronto Blue Jays , and Cleveland Guardians .

Losing outfielder Luis Robert Jr. to the injured list won't help. Robert appeared in just three games with the Orioles following his waiver claim from the New York Mets .

He landed on the injured list with a left hamstring strain. To take his place, the Orioles promoted outfielder Heston Kjerstad from Triple-A Norfolk.

The Athletic's Andy McCullough believes this could be a huge opportunity for Kjerstad, who had a 59 OPS+ in 54 games with the Orioles in 2025.

"Less than a week after Baltimore spent $5 million to claim him off waivers, Robert injured his hamstring. So it goes," McCullough wrote.

"That could mean more at-bats for Kjerstad, who has never put it all together since being chosen at No. 2 overall in 2020," McCullough added.

Kjerstad had solid offensive numbers in Triple-A, hitting .289/.337/.462 with 11 home runs and a .799 OPS in 79 games.

The 27-year-old may not be Baltimore's savior and lead the organization back to the postseason.

But he could make a lasting impression on the coaching staff and front office with a strong September. Robert's unfortunate injury paved the way for playing time for Kjerstad.

articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup players' hotel evacuated after fire breaks out ahead of high-stakes final stage
articles.summary: A fire in a neighboring parking facility forced Women's Basketball World Cup teams out of their Berlin hotel for the second time in three days.
articles.body: Women’s Basketball World Cup teams were forced to evacuate their Berlin hotel early Tuesday morning for the second time in three days, after a fire started in a neighboring parking facility. FIBA said the alarm went off at 9:06 a.m. local time. The teams followed standard safety procedures and assembled outside before returning to their rooms at 9:27 a.m. "Following a thorough inspection, it was confirmed that the alarm was activated due to the start of a fire in the garbage room located in the underground basement of a neighbouring parking facility," FIBA said in a statement. "The Police are currently investigating the exact circumstances surrounding the incident." The U.S. team was not affected because the Americans are staying at a different hotel from the rest of the tournament field. WNBA STAR WILL MISS PLAYING IN FIBA WORLD CUP AFTER HER PASSPORT GOES MISSING IN THE MAIL The incident came two days after an alarm forced players and coaches out of the same hotel at approximately 2 a.m. Sunday. That evacuation lasted about an hour and disrupted the sleep of teams scheduled to play later that day. FIBA said Tuesday that the first alarm "was due to steam in the kitchen during its cleaning." Australia coach Sandy Brondello had previously said she was told someone activated an emergency alarm in an elevator, according to The Associated Press. THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE Tuesday’s evacuation occurred on the opening day of the knockout stage. Hungary and Japan were scheduled to play the first qualification game, followed by host Germany against South Korea. The winners will advance to face the U.S. and Belgium, respectively, in Thursday’s quarterfinals. FIBA did not report any injuries or changes to the tournament schedule. articles.title: North Carolina Tar Heels Basketball 2026-27 Preview
articles.summary: Just like their football program did in 2025, North Carolina basketball is in the midst of a complete overhaul. Can former long-time NBA head coach Michael M...
articles.body:
Just like their football program did in 2025, North Carolina basketball is in the midst of a complete overhaul. Can former long-time NBA head coach Michael Malone get the Tar Heels back to being serious NCAA title contenders?

UNC surprisingly fired Hubert Davis this offseason, and more problematic, the Tar Heels didn't have a plan. The Tar Heels parted ways with Davis, who was under contract through 2030, despite going 125-54 under him, which included four NCAA Tournaments and an appearance in the 2022 national championship game. The Heels won 20 or more games in each of the five seasons and won the ACC regular season crown in 2024. Granted, they failed to get out of the first round of the NCAA Tournament the past two years.

Now, UNC turns to Malone. Malone, who led the Denver Nuggets to the 2023 NBA championship, has never been a college head coach. However, the 54-year-old — who played at Loyola (Maryland) — was a collegiate assistant from 1994-2001. He has a 510-394 career record.

Not only has Malone had to assemble a new coaching staff, but he has also had to rebuild the Tar Heels' roster. Malone did retain Sean May, Pat Sullivan and Eric Hoots from Davis' staff. Only five players from last year's squad, which went 24-9 and finished fourth in the ACC at 12-6, return.

Carolina lost Caleb Wilson and Henri Veesar to the NBA, along with Seth Trimble, who was recently ruled temporarily eligible for a fifth year and will play for Louisville in 2026-27. Malone also saw Derek Dixon (Arizona), Luka Bogavac , and Jonathan Powell transfer.

Senior forward Jair Stevenson is the main returnee. Jaydon Young and Isaiah Denis also return and could be in the mix for playing time off the bench.

Stevenson produced a career year in his first year in Chapel Hill after transferring from Alabama, and he stepped up his production during ACC play. Overall, he averaged 8.1 points and 4.4 rebounds (1.4 offensive) with shooting splits of 47.0/29.5/74.2.

Stevenson projects as a key piece of Malone's rotation, whether he comes off the bench or starts. The 6-10 forward, a former North Carolina Gatorade Player of the Year, is a high-IQ perimeter defender who can play either the 3 or 4.

Young struggled this past year in his first season at Chapel Hill after a decent sophomore campaign at Virginia Tech. The 6-4 combo guard could be in the mix for a rotation spot as a high-energy defensive spark off the bench.

Denis, the consensus No. 64 recruit in the class of 2025, only saw 33 minutes in 10 games last season. The 6-3 guard is an athletic slasher with a quick first step and defensive upside.

Malone has also brought in 11 newcomers with six transfers, four freshmen, and one international player. According to Inside Carolina, the Tar Heels have spent over $20 million on their new-look roster.

Matt Able , Neo Avdalas, and Terrence Brown headline the transfers. Able, the consensus No. 20 recruit in 2025, came off the bench for NC State last year and tested the NBA waters before deciding to land in Chapel Hill. Able projects to start on the wing for Malone and brings athleticism and shooting to the Tar Heels.

Avdalas, the No.84 recruit in 2024, had a solid freshman campaign at Virginia Tech. Avdalas, from Greece, projects as a Tar Heel backcourt starter, with excellent court vision and playmaking ability. He thrives in transition and pick-and-rolls.

Brown is a high-volume, versatile scorer who has averaged 20 points a game over the last two years —compiling 19.9 points, 3.8 assists, and 1.4 steals with shooting splits of 45.3/32.7/77.5 in 2025-26 at Utah. The 6-3 combo guard is at his best when getting downhill, as he has an explosive first step and is also a capable facilitator. He is also a fierce defender who can guard either backcourt position.

Buffalo transfer Angelo Brizzi and South Dakota transfer Cameron Fens also figure to be a major part of Malone's rotation. However, Fens' eligibility is in question, as is that of several other players, following the Tennessee Court of Appeals ' order granting a stay of the injunction last week.

"Cameron [Fens] is, simply stated, eligible to work out, practice, lift and condition," Malone recently said. "He's a huge part of our team right now. All of those things will take care of themselves in the coming weeks. But the luxury that we have is that he is cleared to practice, play and be a part of this team."

Brizzi has improved each of his collegiate seasons and is coming off a career year, though he has moved around quite a bit—UNC is his fifth stop. While he is not a creator, the 6-3 guard is a good shooter off the catch and did a better job of drawing free throws this past campaign. He also has quick hands and does a good job as a help defender.

Malone's first recruiting class is pretty solid, with On3 ranking it the third best in the ACC and 18th in the country. Maximo Adams and Sayon Keita are the crown jewels of the recruiting class.

Adams is a big, versatile wing who is a three-level scorer and a strong rebounder. Adams possesses outstanding footwork and is at his best when operating out of the mid-range. The 6-7 forward excels at cutting to the basket and relocating to open spots. Additionally, he can guard 2-4 and should be a major contributor off the bench.

Keita is a long, athletic, 7-foot center with a 7-7 wingspan who thrives as a rim-runner and pick-and-roll. Keita is also an outstanding rebounder and rim-protector. The Mali native spent the last three seasons in the Barcelona pipeline, seeing limited time this past year with Barca — appearing in 15 games in Spanish ACB and EuroLeague contests, including four starts. He is expected to compete with 6-11 Greek center Alexandros Samodurov.

Samodurov spent the last four years in the Panathinaikos system, where he spent the last two-plus seasons with the main team in limited minutes. Samodurov is an athletic, versatile big who can shoot, handle, and attack. He averaged 3.1 points on 53.1% shooting and 1.5 rebounds in nine minutes for Panathinaikos this past year.

Thomas comes to the Tar Heels highly touted due to his athleticism and size. A high-flyer, Thomas thrives in the open court, though he is a capable producer in the half-court due to his cutting, passing, and decision-making ability.

Jaydon Young, Cade Bennerman, Malloy Smith, Evan Smith, John Holbrook

UNC has three preseason games against Southern California, Indiana, and Charlotte. The Tar Heels open their nonconference schedule with six straight home games, the most intriguing of which is against Georgia. Overall, they will host nine of their 14 opponents, with Butler and Arkansas (ACC/SEC Challenge) being the only other high-major opponents.

Carolina's only true road game is at Georgetown on December 12. The Heels do have some interesting neutral court contests. UNC's neutral court contests include West Virginia in Charlotte (Dick Vitale Invitational), Kentucky in New York (CBS Sports Classic), and Illinois in Nashville (Nashville Hoops Showdown).

For their 2026-27 ACC schedule, UNC will play home-and-away series against Duke and Louisville. The Tar Heels will not face Clemson this year.

The Tar Heels will also host: California, Georgia Tech, Miami, NC State, SMU, Stanford and Virginia.

The Heels' other road games: Boston College, Florida State, Notre Dame, Pittsburgh, Syracuse Virginia Tech, Wake Forest

articles.title: New Jimmy Butler Rumors Reveal 'Notable Progress' in Knee Injury Recovery, Targeted Return Timeline
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler has made "notable progress" in his recovery from the surgical reconstruction of his right ACL he underwent six months ago, ESPN's Anthony Slater reported Tuesday.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler has made "notable progress" in his recovery from the surgical reconstruction of his right ACL he underwent six months ago, ESPN's Anthony Slater reported Tuesday.

Slater reported Butler "has been slowly increasing his on-court work" but won't be a full participant in training camp as he "still has extensive rehab work ahead."

"He is expected to be limited to individual court and strength work when training camp opens in a month, league sources said, with the 36-year-old forward needing more time to be cleared for a full contact setting," Slater reported.

An "optimistic target" for Butler's return would be January or February 2027, according to Slater.

That would mark a year away from NBA action for Butler, who suffered his torn ACL Jan. 19 and underwent surgery Feb. 9.

The Warriors are set to hold training camp Sept. 29 through Oct. 3 in Oahu, Hawaii.

The team is set to open the preseason Oct. 4 against the Los Angeles Clippers before tipping off the regular season Oct. 21 at the Los Angeles Lakers.

ClutchPoints' Brett Siegel reported last month it "appears very likely" Butler would be back on the floor for the Warriors before the trade deadline on Feb. 11, 2027.

According to Siegel, the Warriors' Dec. 25 matchup against the Denver Nuggets "seems to be the earliest date mentioned in conversations as a 'Hey, you never know' type of target date, but nothing is definitive."

Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy has already confirmed the Warriors are expecting to be without both Butler and Moses Moody, who underwent left knee surgery in March, for at least the opening stretch of the 2026-27 season.

The Athletic's Marcus Thompson II reported last month Moody is "targeting September to resume running and returning to on-court work."

Losing Butler and Moody after missing both Stephen Curry and Kristaps Porziņģis for extended stretches of the 2025-26 season contributed to the Warriors' elimination from last spring's play-in round.

Potentially getting both Moody and Butler back on the court by February could give the Warriors a better shot at evaluating before the next trade deadline whether a healthier version of this roster should have improved postseason hopes.

articles.title: New Kawhi Leonard Rumors Update Timeline for Clippers-Raptors Trade to Be Finalized After NBA Probe
articles.summary: With the NBA's investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers complete, the question now is when Kawhi Leonard will be on his way to the Toronto Raptors following a trade agreement earlier this offseason.
articles.body:
With the NBA's investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers complete, the question now is when Kawhi Leonard will be on his way to the Toronto Raptors following a trade agreement earlier this offseason.

NBA insider Jake Fischer reported Tuesday that the trade has not been finalized because the Clippers are still restructuring their front office after team owner Steve Ballmer and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank received suspensions.

Fischer noted that Leonard has been in Miami for an organized minicamp with other Raptors players.

The Clippers agreed to trade Leonard to the Raptors on June 30 in return for forward Brandon Ingram, guard Gradey Dick, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 and rights to a first-round pick swap in 2027, but the league had to conclude its investigation before the deal was finalized.

After the NBA found that the Clippers had violated the salary cap circumvention rules, Leonard was fined $700,000. Ballmer was suspended from all league and team activities for a year, while Lawrence was dealt a six-month suspension.

Los Angeles also had to forfeit five first-round draft picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033.

Shortly after the league announced the punishments, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the trade was still expected to go through.

"There's full expectation that this trade will be going down as is between the Clippers and the Raptors that had multiple first-round picks, other swaps and second-round pick considerations going to the Clippers," Charania reported on SportsCenter . "The trade is on track and both sides can now move forward with getting this deal done."

While there has been no indication that either side plans to back out of the trade, it seems there will be a waiting period before it is completed. The Raptors begin training camp at the end of the month and presumably prefer for Leonard to be on the roster by then.

Once Leonard joins Toronto, it will mark a reunion between the two sides after seven years apart. Leonard's sole season with the Raptors in 2018-19 ended with a championship, and he's looking for a similar result this time around.

While the Raptors are gearing up for what should be a good season, the Clippers are likely looking at a down year without Leonard, and forfeiting five first-rounders will make their rebuild even harder.

articles.title: Georgia Bulldogs place game one highlights behind paywall as post-NIL college football becomes more soulless
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs posted a game highlight film behind a $20 paywall on a third-party site called Glory Glory, and fans are furious about it.
articles.body: I read your comments. I read all of them. Every time I post an article about college football, I scroll down to the comments section to see what the readers are talking about. And it doesn't matter if the article is about Dabo Swinney going down with the ship at Clemson or Texas Tech's stiffest competition in the Big 12, the majority of the comments are always the same. SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE "Who cares? NIL has ruined the sport anyway." Most of the time, I just roll my eyes and move on with my day. College football is my favorite sport, and although NIL and unlimited player movement — among other things — has made the sport more of a headache to follow, I will still gleefully park my butt in front of my television on Saturday morning and try to soak up as many games as I can. This latest development, however, may have me joining the doomsday prophets in the comments section. The Georgia Bulldogs played a game against an overmatched opponent this past Saturday. It doesn't matter who, because they kicked the crap out of them. COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS After the game, the football team's official X account posted a teaser trailer for their week one highlight film, complete with a link to go see the whole thing. There was just one problem: the video is behind a $20 paywall. The worst part is that the link doesn't even take fans to the UGA athletic department's website, but rather a third-party site called Glory Glory. Glory Glory is described as "a fan-first ecosystem designed to capture and share exclusive content, deliver unparalleled access to UGA athletics, and inspire deeper levels of engagement." In layman's terms (at least how I understand it), you pay money to this site which then goes towards the players' NIL funds, and in turn, the fans get team-related content and access. Judging by the comments underneath the video, this is a nearly universally reviled practice, and I can't blame them. Where does it end? HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL We have rev share. We have NIL collectives. We even have places like Tennessee implementing "talent fees" on season tickets that go towards, you guessed it, NIL. This is all in addition to millionaire and billionaire boosters footing large portions of the NIL bill as it stands. None of this is sustainable, and it's why places like the federal government have become battlegrounds to try and "save college sports." No one likes this, yet it will continue to happen. I can't see myself ever losing my love for college football; I'm too indoctrinated at this point. I am, what many would call, a "sicko." But a large portion of fans are already becoming disillusioned with the sport, and it's things like Georgia's paywall tactic that are inflicting the bulk of the damage. The death of college football may happen by way of "death by 1,000 papercuts," and we are already a couple hundred cuts deep. articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Updated Qualified Teams, Schedule, Odds, Bracket Predictions
articles.summary: Team USA will take on Hungary for a spot in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup semifinals.
articles.body:
Team USA will take on Hungary for a spot in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup semifinals.

Hungary earned a trip to the quarterfinals Tuesday after claiming victory over Japan in Berlin.

Germany later secured its own quarterfinal bid in front of the home crowd with a blowout victory over Korea.

Caitlin Clark sets unwanted personal record in FIBA World Cup

Here's a look at the updated bracket, upcoming schedule, odds and predictions as the knockout rounds continue this week in Berlin.

Hungary began the World Cup with a blowout loss to France before bouncing back with wins over Nigeria, Korea and Japan on their way to the quarterfinals.

France shot 62.5 percent from the field in that tournament-opening victory.

Leaning on stars who can contribute that same kind of efficient offense, like Paige Bueckers and her 59.1 percent shooting rate from the field, could be key to the United States' hopes of making it past Hungary and into the semifinals.

Germany similarly opened the tournament with a big loss to Spain before bouncing back with wins over Japan, Mali and Korea.

Belgium, which has cruised to double-digit wins over Turkïye, Puerto Rico and Austria, arguably presents Germany's toughest opponent of the tournament so far.

Leonie Fiebich recorded three blocks in Tuesday's win over Korea. More strong defense from Fiebich and a supportive home crowd could help Germany stymy one of the tournament's highest-scoring teams.
